answer: Convex per-identity bonding resists sybils: the bond to register climbs superlinearly with how many identities trace to one funding root — the first key costs little, the hundredth far more. A delta of clones minted off one capital source pays a steep convex sum, not a hundred flat bonds, while a garden of genuinely independent agents each pays only the low first-key price. Precondition: funding provenance is traceable on-ledger, anchoring the curve to a root; the ivory assumption that clones are cheap then inverts.
